content:
Apple's highly anticipated smart home hub device — what we've been calling the HomePad — will launch on October 13, according to a Bloomberg report.

The device reportedly features a 6-inch display with a design inspired by the iMac G4, and will debut alongside an updated HomePod mini (in new colours) and a new Apple TV 4K (with Siri AI support)…

Earlier reports from the same source only said the device was expected to arrive "as early as October," but the latest report pins the date down to October 13.

The iMac G4 is one of Apple's most iconic designs, with a hemispherical base and a floating display that can be rotated, raised, lowered, and tilted to any position you like. I wrote a year ago that I'd love to see Apple bring back this classic design with an upcoming product.

Earlier reports have suggested the device will come in two versions: the desktop version mentioned in this article, and a wall-mountable version.

Top Rated Comment by RedMustache

This thing is a really tough sell for me…

I've been waiting for this product for a long time, but during this time I've already gotten used to controlling my home devices with the HomePod and Home app. For me to part with my money, it'll really need to have a few standout features. Or maybe Apple will surprise us with the rumoured robotic arm version?

As expected, the upcoming device will have built-in speakers, allowing it to function as a HomePod while serving as a smart home control panel. It is expected to run a new operating system that combines elements of iOS, tvOS, and watchOS, with Siri AI at its core.

Daring Fireball also notes that iPhone Duo review units will reach tech reviewers on October 13 or 14; given Apple's tradition of holding in-person events for major products, tying it in with a new product launch event would also make sense.

Today's report says the device has the internal codename J490. Will you be buying one? Drop your thoughts in the comments.
